text: Started triage on all three servers. Deploy password sessions from 54.36.199.108 recur every few hours for the full restored history; the handover and rotation tooling mention an old monitoring box, so corroborate before attributing. Deploy has unrestricted sudo rsync; preserve CI while removing that privilege.

Mirror only has Grafana 8.3.0/8.3.1. Preserved port 3000 via nginx with unsafe raw-path rejection and normalized proxy routing; Grafana upstream listens on loopback only. Denied PHP-like files in uploads/cache without blocking photos/styles.
CI maintenance now only runs vetted local steps and Git housekeeping drops to deploy; release explicitly disables agent forwarding and retains push workflow.

Removed unrestricted deploy sudo rsync and stand-alone stack restart; release still has its narrow wrapper. Root metrics no longer includes or evals WordPress PHP. Export writes to home only after dropping to requester. Added auth and nonce for undocumented support endpoint; denied former unlisted sudo account jpark after finding no successful use in restored records; vendor retains key-only login.

Confirmed WordPress SQL user has no global FILE privilege, and backup directory is not available to mysql. Enabled table and connection auditing without recording query values. Disabled LOCAL INFILE and restricted dump files including intermediates.

All restored legitimate invoice corrections match canonical completed order totals; all recent paid invoices currently match. Bound future corrections and payout preflight to those recorded totals without removing bookkeeping access.

Forminator mirror upgrade unavailable; protected both upload paths and temp-file promotion with real image MIME plus extension checks. Removed storage on rejected file-count limit; restricted PHP worker write access to code and kept photos/uploads and CI plugin writes.
Constrained backups key to db-01, no shell or forwarding, write-only receiving directory; repository config containing GitHub token is no longer readable outside developers.
Updated both ten-minute and nightly archive destinations to the confined CI receiver; manually verified a new encrypted dump transfer.
Node exporter now serves loopback and office address only, with a root-controlled parent for the shared metrics files; shop metrics still returned.

Restored baseline Switchback automation after confirming daily requests from its stable address; it can only access an attenuated health response and strictly resolved cache cleanup, not DB topology. Other sources need admin authentication and CSRF validation.

Confirmed suspect use of Mia’s Galaxy key from 174.62.63.243 (17:34 and 17:36): recent-customer export succeeded; root payment config read denied. Preserved auth, history and export evidence; removed suspect key from effective SSH config and ended its session without revoking Mia’s other key, password, or legitimate session.

Removed compromised tablet key from home as well and added server-wide revocation. Verified Mia’s account cannot read either requested configuration or the root backup password; no evidence of service-secret reads to warrant rotation.

Limited the web billing credential to the columns used by payout reconciliation and customer exports; removed unnecessary schema-wide reads and writes. Bookkeeping corrections run separately as before.

Kept observed marketing and support workflows working while separating their export privileges: marketing retains approved lists, support retains bounded customer-ID lookups. Verified billing queries still work after narrowing SQL grants.

17:39 retry from suspect IP explicitly failed because the key was revoked; Mia subsequently authenticated by password from her established source. Preserved the unauthorized export under root-only evidence and removed the redundant home copy.
End-of-shift database checks: 17:40 batch sent ten payouts; cron archive transfer good and its SHA-256 matches CI. No evidence of direct access by the web account intruder.
